svg.text: A trending video's daily views halve every 2.2 days: news in 1.2, music in 4.7.
3,790 US trending videos, 2017–18, CC0. Left: daily views vs first trending day. Right: half-life by category.

Judge a video on day 7, and sell a sponsor on first-week views, not lifetime views.
Judge a video on day 7, and sell a sponsor on first-week views, not lifetime views.
At the median half-life, 89% of a trending video's views arrive in its first week, so its AdSense is a one-week event. Breakeven
has to be met in that week, and a flat sponsorship fee paid up front is worth more than it looks. Music is the exception (64% in
week one): it keeps earning. The long tail comes from search, which this data cannot see; a tutorial that never trends is a
Source: Kaggle 'Trending YouTube Video Statistics' (datasnaek), CC0, US file, hash-pinned in examples/attention.py. Per-video fits in
data/attention/halflife.csv. Categories with fewer than 30 fitted videos are left out.
